data.title: Attacker Artefacts Removed Without Trace
data.summary:
Files, shell history and other artefacts created during the engagement were removed from
compromised hosts, and nothing recorded their creation or deletion.
data.description:
Where the only record of activity lives on the host that was compromised, that record is
within the attacker's control. Cleanup then removes the organisation's ability to scope an
incident: not just whether it happened, but which systems and which data were reached.

Scoping is the practical cost. An organisation that detects an intrusion but cannot
establish its extent must assume the worst across the estate, which turns a contained
incident into an expensive one.

The engagement's own cleanup is a reasonable proxy for an adversary's, and the finding is
usually best expressed as what the client would have been able to reconstruct afterwards
— in this case, very little.
data.recommendation:
* Forward process, file and authentication telemetry off-host so the record survives the
  host.
* Retain it for a period matched to realistic dwell time rather than to storage
  convenience.
* Test the ability to reconstruct a timeline from forwarded data alone, as part of incident
  response exercises.
data.short_recommendation: Forward telemetry off-host and test timeline reconstruction without the host.
